title: JEE Advanced 2024 · Paper 1
instr: Official JEE (Advanced) 2024 Paper 1 with the final answer key published by the organising IIT (IIT Madras).
51 questions: Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry, 17 in each subject, in four sections. Total 180 marks.
Section 1 – single correct option: +3 if correct, −1 if wrong, 0 if not answered.
Section 2 – one or more correct options: +4 if you choose all the correct options; +3 / +2 / +1 if you choose only some of the correct options and no wrong one; −2 in all other cases.
Section 3 – numerical answer (a non-negative integer): +4 if correct, no negative marks.
Section 4 – List-I / List-II matching (one correct option): +3 if correct, −1 if wrong.
source: JEE (Advanced) 2024 question paper and final answer key, organising IIT (IIT Madras). Worked solutions: All in All Exam Practice.

questions.text: Let $f(x)$ be a continuously differentiable function on the interval $(0, \infty)$ such that $f(1) = 2$ and $$\lim_{t \to x} \frac{t^{10} f(x) - x^{10} f(t)}{t^9 - x^9} = 1$$ for each $x > 0$. Then, for all $x > 0$, $f(x)$ is equal to
questions.sol:
The limit is of the form $\dfrac00$; by L'Hospital's rule (differentiating in $t$): $\dfrac{10x^9 f(x) - x^{10} f'(x)}{9x^8} = 1$.
So $10x f(x) - x^2 f'(x) = 9$, i.e. $f'(x) - \dfrac{10}{x} f(x) = -\dfrac{9}{x^2}$.
Integrating factor $x^{-10}$: $\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(x^{-10} f(x)\right) = -9x^{-12} \Rightarrow x^{-10} f(x) = \dfrac{9}{11}x^{-11} + K$.
So $f(x) = \dfrac{9}{11x} + Kx^{10}$; $f(1) = 2 \Rightarrow K = \dfrac{13}{11}$.
$f(x) = \dfrac{9}{11x} + \dfrac{13}{11}x^{10}$ → (B).

questions.text: A student appears for a quiz consisting of only true-false type questions and answers all the questions. The student knows the answers of some questions and guesses the answers for the remaining questions. Whenever the student knows the answer of a question, he gives the correct answer. Assume that the probability of the student giving the correct answer for a question, given that he has guessed it, is $\dfrac{1}{2}$. Also assume that the probability of the answer for a question being guessed, given that the student's answer is correct, is $\dfrac{1}{6}$. Then the probability that the student knows the answer of a randomly chosen question is
questions.sol:
Let $p$ = P(knows). Then P(guesses) $= 1-p$.
P(correct) $= p\cdot1 + (1-p)\cdot\dfrac12 = \dfrac{1+p}{2}$.
P(guessed $\mid$ correct) $= \dfrac{(1-p)/2}{(1+p)/2} = \dfrac{1-p}{1+p} = \dfrac16$.
$6 - 6p = 1 + p \Rightarrow p = \dfrac57$ → (C).

questions.text: Let $\dfrac{\pi}{2} \lt x \lt \pi$ be such that $\cot x = \dfrac{-5}{\sqrt{11}}$. Then $$\left(\sin\frac{11x}{2}\right)\left(\sin 6x - \cos 6x\right) + \left(\cos\frac{11x}{2}\right)\left(\sin 6x + \cos 6x\right)$$ is equal to
questions.sol:
Let $a = \dfrac{11x}{2}$. Regroup: $(\sin 6x\cos a - \cos 6x\sin a) + (\cos 6x\cos a + \sin 6x\sin a) = \sin(6x - a) + \cos(6x - a)$.
$6x - a = \dfrac{x}{2}$, so the expression is $\sin\dfrac{x}{2} + \cos\dfrac{x}{2}$.
$\csc^2 x = 1 + \dfrac{25}{11} = \dfrac{36}{11}$; $x$ in the second quadrant gives $\sin x = \dfrac{\sqrt{11}}{6}$, $\cos x = -\dfrac56$.
$\dfrac{x}{2} \in \left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$: $\cos\dfrac{x}{2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{1+\cos x}{2}} = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt3}$, $\sin\dfrac{x}{2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{1-\cos x}{2}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{11}}{2\sqrt3}$.
Sum $= \dfrac{\sqrt{11}+1}{2\sqrt3}$ → (B).

questions.text: Consider the ellipse $\dfrac{x^2}{9} + \dfrac{y^2}{4} = 1$. Let $S(p, q)$ be a point in the first quadrant such that $\dfrac{p^2}{9} + \dfrac{q^2}{4} > 1$. Two tangents are drawn from $S$ to the ellipse, of which one meets the ellipse at one end point of the minor axis and the other meets the ellipse at a point $T$ in the fourth quadrant. Let $R$ be the vertex of the ellipse with positive $x$-coordinate and $O$ be the center of the ellipse. If the area of the triangle $\Delta ORT$ is $\dfrac{3}{2}$, then which of the following options is correct?
questions.sol:
$S$ is in the first quadrant, so the tangent at an end of the minor axis is the one at $(0, 2)$, namely $y = 2$; hence $q = 2$.
$R = (3, 0)$, so area $ORT = \dfrac12 \cdot 3 \cdot |y_T| = \dfrac32 \Rightarrow y_T = -1$ (fourth quadrant), and $x_T = 3\sqrt{1 - \dfrac14} = \dfrac{3\sqrt3}{2}$.
Tangent at $T$: $\dfrac{x}{9}\cdot\dfrac{3\sqrt3}{2} - \dfrac{y}{4} = 1$, i.e. $\dfrac{\sqrt3}{6}x - \dfrac{y}{4} = 1$.
It passes through $S(p, 2)$: $\dfrac{\sqrt3}{6}p = \dfrac32 \Rightarrow p = 3\sqrt3$ → (A).

questions.text: Let $S = \left\{a + b\sqrt{2} : a, b \in \mathbb{Z}\right\}$, $T_1 = \left\{\left(-1+\sqrt{2}\right)^n : n \in \mathbb{N}\right\}$, and $T_2 = \left\{\left(1+\sqrt{2}\right)^n : n \in \mathbb{N}\right\}$. Then which of the following statements is (are) TRUE?
options: For any given $a, b \in \mathbb{Z}$, $\cos\left(\pi\left(a + b\sqrt{2}\right)\right) + i\sin\left(\pi\left(a + b\sqrt{2}\right)\right) \in \mathbb{Z}$ if and only if $b = 0$, where $i = \sqrt{-1}$.
questions.sol:
(A) $\mathbb{Z} \subset S$ ($b = 0$), and $S$ is closed under multiplication, so every power of $-1+\sqrt2 \in S$ and of $1+\sqrt2 \in S$ lies in $S$. TRUE.
(B) $0 \lt \sqrt2 - 1 \lt 1$, so $(\sqrt2-1)^n \to 0$ and some power lies in $\left(0, \dfrac{1}{2024}\right)$. FALSE.
(C) $1 + \sqrt2 > 1$, so $(1+\sqrt2)^n \to \infty$ and exceeds 2024. TRUE.
(D) The number is $e^{i\pi\theta}$ with $\theta = a + b\sqrt2$; it has modulus 1, so it is an integer only if it is $\pm1$, i.e. $\theta \in \mathbb{Z}$. As $\sqrt2$ is irrational, this happens if and only if $b = 0$. TRUE.
Answer: (A), (C), (D).

questions.text: Let $\mathbb{R}^2$ denote $\mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R}$. Let $$S = \left\{(a, b, c) : a, b, c \in \mathbb{R} \text{ and } ax^2 + 2bxy + cy^2 > 0 \text{ for all } (x, y) \in \mathbb{R}^2 - \{(0,0)\}\right\}.$$Then which of the following statements is (are) TRUE?
options: For any given $(a, b, c) \in S$, the system of linear equations $$ax + by = 1, \quad bx + cy = -1$$ has a unique solution.
For any given $(a, b, c) \in S$, the system of linear equations $$(a+1)x + by = 0, \quad bx + (c+1)y = 0$$ has a unique solution.
questions.sol:
$ax^2 + 2bxy + cy^2 > 0$ for all $(x, y) \neq (0, 0)$ exactly when $a > 0$ and $ac - b^2 > 0$ (then also $c > 0$).
(A) $ac - b^2 = 12 - \dfrac{49}{4} \lt 0$. FALSE.
(B) $3 \cdot \dfrac{1}{12} > b^2 \Rightarrow b^2 \lt \dfrac14 \Rightarrow |2b| \lt 1$. TRUE.
(C) The determinant of the system is $ac - b^2 > 0$, so the solution is unique. TRUE.
(D) Determinant $(a+1)(c+1) - b^2 = (ac - b^2) + a + c + 1 > 0$, so the solution is unique. TRUE.
Answer: (B), (C), (D).

questions.text: Let $\mathbb{R}^3$ denote the three-dimensional space. Take two points $P = (1, 2, 3)$ and $Q = (4, 2, 7)$. Let $dist(X, Y)$ denote the distance between two points $X$ and $Y$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$. Let $$S = \left\{X \in \mathbb{R}^3 : \left(dist(X, P)\right)^2 - \left(dist(X, Q)\right)^2 = 50\right\}$$ and $$T = \left\{Y \in \mathbb{R}^3 : \left(dist(Y, Q)\right)^2 - \left(dist(Y, P)\right)^2 = 50\right\}.$$Then which of the following statements is (are) TRUE?
options: There is a triangle whose area is 1 and all of whose vertices are from $S$.
There are two distinct points $L$ and $M$ in $T$ such that each point on the line segment $LM$ is also in $T$.
There are infinitely many rectangles of perimeter 48, two of whose vertices are from $S$ and the other two vertices are from $T$.
There is a square of perimeter 48, two of whose vertices are from $S$ and the other two vertices are from $T$.
questions.sol:
For $X = (x, y, z)$: $|X-P|^2 - |X-Q|^2 = 2X\cdot(Q - P) + |P|^2 - |Q|^2$, with $Q - P = (3, 0, 4)$, $|P|^2 = 14$, $|Q|^2 = 69$.
$S$: $6x + 8z - 55 = 50$, i.e. the plane $6x + 8z = 105$. $T$: $-(6x + 8z) + 55 = 50$, i.e. the plane $6x + 8z = 5$.
(A), (B): $S$ and $T$ are planes, so they contain triangles of any area and whole line segments. TRUE.
The planes are parallel, at distance $\dfrac{105 - 5}{\sqrt{36 + 64}} = 10$.
(C) Take a rectangle with two sides joining the planes (each of length $\ell \ge 10$, at a suitable slant) and the other two sides of length $24 - \ell$ parallel to the planes. Any $\ell \in [10, 24)$ (and any position) works: infinitely many. TRUE.
(D) A square of perimeter 48 has side $12 \ge 10$, so the same construction with $\ell = 12$ works. TRUE.
Answer: (A), (B), (C), (D).

questions.text: Let $f(x) = x^4 + ax^3 + bx^2 + c$ be a polynomial with real coefficients such that $f(1) = -9$. Suppose that $i\sqrt{3}$ is a root of the equation $4x^3 + 3ax^2 + 2bx = 0$, where $i = \sqrt{-1}$. If $\alpha_1, \alpha_2, \alpha_3$, and $\alpha_4$ are all the roots of the equation $f(x) = 0$, then $|\alpha_1|^2 + |\alpha_2|^2 + |\alpha_3|^2 + |\alpha_4|^2$ is equal to ______.
questions.sol:
$4x^3 + 3ax^2 + 2bx = x(4x^2 + 3ax + 2b)$; with real coefficients, $\pm i\sqrt3$ are the roots of $4x^2 + 3ax + 2b = 0$.
Sum of roots $0 \Rightarrow a = 0$; product $3 = \dfrac{2b}{4} \Rightarrow b = 6$.
$f(1) = 1 + 6 + c = -9 \Rightarrow c = -16$, so $f(x) = x^4 + 6x^2 - 16 = (x^2 - 2)(x^2 + 8)$.
Roots $\pm\sqrt2$ and $\pm 2\sqrt2\, i$: $|\alpha|^2 = 2, 2, 8, 8$.
Sum $= 20$.

questions.text: Let $$S = \left\{A = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 1 & c \\ 1 & a & d \\ 1 & b & e \end{pmatrix} : a, b, c, d, e \in \{0, 1\} \text{ and } |A| \in \{-1, 1\}\right\},$$ where $|A|$ denotes the determinant of $A$. Then the number of elements in $S$ is _______.
questions.sol:
Expanding along the first row: $|A| = -1\cdot(e - d) + c(b - a) = (d - e) + c(b - a)$.
$c = 0$: need $d - e = \pm1$: 2 choices of $(d, e)$, $a, b$ free (4) → 8 matrices.
$c = 1$: need $(d - e) + (b - a) = \pm1$. Each difference is $0$ (2 ways) or $\pm1$ (1 way each).
One difference $0$ and the other $\pm1$: $2 \times 2 + 2 \times 2 = 8$ matrices (the two $\pm1$ cases give sums $0$ or $\pm2$).
Total $= 8 + 8 = 16$.

questions.text: A group of 9 students, $s_1, s_2, \ldots, s_9$, is to be divided to form three teams $X, Y$, and $Z$ of sizes 2, 3, and 4, respectively. Suppose that $s_1$ cannot be selected for the team $X$, and $s_2$ cannot be selected for the team $Y$. Then the number of ways to form such teams, is _______.
questions.sol:
Without restrictions: $\dfrac{9!}{2!\,3!\,4!} = 1260$.
$s_1 \in X$: choose 1 more for $X$ from 8 and 3 for $Y$ from 7: $8 \times 35 = 280$.
$s_2 \in Y$: choose 2 for $X$ from 8 and 2 more for $Y$ from 6: $28 \times 15 = 420$.
Both: 1 more for $X$ from 7, 2 more for $Y$ from 6: $7 \times 15 = 105$.
Required $= 1260 - 280 - 420 + 105 = 665$.

questions.text: Let $\overrightarrow{OP} = \dfrac{\alpha - 1}{\alpha}\hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k}$, $\overrightarrow{OQ} = \hat{i} + \dfrac{\beta - 1}{\beta}\hat{j} + \hat{k}$ and $\overrightarrow{OR} = \hat{i} + \hat{j} + \dfrac{1}{2}\hat{k}$ be three vectors, where $\alpha, \beta \in \mathbb{R} - \{0\}$ and $O$ denotes the origin. If $\left(\overrightarrow{OP} \times \overrightarrow{OQ}\right) \cdot \overrightarrow{OR} = 0$ and the point $(\alpha, \beta, 2)$ lies on the plane $3x + 3y - z + l = 0$, then the value of $l$ is ________.
questions.sol:
Let $p = 1 - \dfrac1\alpha$, $q = 1 - \dfrac1\beta$. Then $\begin{vmatrix} p & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & q & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & \frac12 \end{vmatrix} = p\left(\dfrac q2 - 1\right) + \dfrac12 + (1 - q) = 0$, i.e. $pq - 2p - 2q + 3 = 0$.
With $u = \dfrac1\alpha$, $v = \dfrac1\beta$: $(1-u)(1-v) - 2(1-u) - 2(1-v) + 3 = uv + u + v = 0$.
Multiplying by $\alpha\beta$: $1 + \beta + \alpha = 0$, so $\alpha + \beta = -1$.
On the plane: $3(\alpha + \beta) - 2 + l = 0 \Rightarrow -3 - 2 + l = 0 \Rightarrow l = 5$.

questions.text: Let $X$ be a random variable, and let $P(X = x)$ denote the probability that $X$ takes the value $x$. Suppose that the points $(x, P(X = x))$, $x = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4$, lie on a fixed straight line in the $xy$-plane, and $P(X = x) = 0$ for all $x \in \mathbb{R} - \{0, 1, 2, 3, 4\}$. If the mean of $X$ is $\dfrac{5}{2}$, and the variance of $X$ is $\alpha$, then the value of $24\alpha$ is ______.
questions.sol:
Let $P(X = x) = mx + k$ for $x = 0, \ldots, 4$.
Total probability: $10m + 5k = 1$. Mean: $\sum x(mx + k) = 30m + 10k = \dfrac52$.
From the first, $10k = 2 - 20m$, so $10m + 2 = \dfrac52 \Rightarrow m = \dfrac{1}{20}$, $k = \dfrac{1}{10}$.
$E(X^2) = m\sum x^3 + k\sum x^2 = \dfrac{100}{20} + \dfrac{30}{10} = 8$.
$\alpha = 8 - \dfrac{25}{4} = \dfrac74$, so $24\alpha = 42$.

questions.text:
Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be the distinct roots of the equation $x^2 + x - 1 = 0$. Consider the set $T = \{1, \alpha, \beta\}$. For a $3 \times 3$ matrix $M = (a_{ij})_{3\times3}$, define $R_i = a_{i1} + a_{i2} + a_{i3}$ and $C_j = a_{1j} + a_{2j} + a_{3j}$ for $i = 1, 2, 3$ and $j = 1, 2, 3$.
Match each entry in List-I to the correct entry in List-II.
List-IList-II
(P) The number of matrices $M = (a_{ij})_{3\times3}$ with all entries in $T$ such that $R_i = C_j = 0$ for all $i, j$, is(1) $1$
(Q) The number of symmetric matrices $M = (a_{ij})_{3\times3}$ with all entries in $T$ such that $C_j = 0$ for all $j$, is(2) $12$
(R) Let $M = (a_{ij})_{3\times3}$ be a skew symmetric matrix such that $a_{ij} \in T$ for $i > j$. Then the number of elements in the set $\left\{\begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \\ z \end{pmatrix} : x, y, z \in \mathbb{R},\ M\begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \\ z \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} a_{12} \\ 0 \\ -a_{23} \end{pmatrix}\right\}$ is(3) infinite
(S) Let $M = (a_{ij})_{3\times3}$ be a matrix with all entries in $T$ such that $R_i = 0$ for all $i$. Then the absolute value of the determinant of $M$ is(4) $6$
(5) $0$
questions.sol:
$\alpha + \beta = -1$, so $1 + \alpha + \beta = 0$. If three entries of $T$ (with repetition) add to 0, say $n_1 + n_2\alpha + n_3\beta = 0$ with $n_1 + n_2 + n_3 = 3$, writing $\alpha, \beta = \dfrac{-1 \pm \sqrt5}{2}$ forces $n_2 = n_3$ and $n_1 = n_2$: the three entries are $1, \alpha, \beta$ in some order.
(P) Every row and column is a permutation of $1, \alpha, \beta$: a $3\times3$ Latin square; there are $12$ → (2).
(Q) Columns are permutations of $T$, and by symmetry so are rows. A symmetric $3\times3$ Latin square has all three symbols on the diagonal ($3! = 6$ ways), and then the off-diagonal entries are forced → $6$ → (4).
(R) $(x, y, z) = (0, 1, 0)$ gives $M(0,1,0)^T = (a_{12}, 0, -a_{23})^T$, so the system is consistent. A $3\times3$ skew symmetric matrix is singular, so the solutions form a line: infinitely many → (3).
(S) $R_i = 0$ means $M(1,1,1)^T = 0$, so $|M| = 0$ → (5).
P→2, Q→4, R→3, S→5 → (C).

questions.text:
Let the straight line $y = 2x$ touch a circle with center $(0, \alpha)$, $\alpha > 0$, and radius $r$ at a point $A_1$. Let $B_1$ be the point on the circle such that the line segment $A_1B_1$ is a diameter of the circle. Let $\alpha + r = 5 + \sqrt{5}$.
Match each entry in List-I to the correct entry in List-II.
List-IList-II
(P) $\alpha$ equals(1) $(-2, 4)$
(Q) $r$ equals(2) $\sqrt{5}$
(R) $A_1$ equals(3) $(-2, 6)$
(S) $B_1$ equals(4) $5$
(5) $(2, 4)$
questions.sol:
Tangency: $r$ = distance of $(0, \alpha)$ from $2x - y = 0$ $= \dfrac{\alpha}{\sqrt5}$.
$\alpha + \dfrac{\alpha}{\sqrt5} = 5 + \sqrt5 = \sqrt5(\sqrt5 + 1) \Rightarrow \alpha\cdot\dfrac{\sqrt5 + 1}{\sqrt5} = \sqrt5(\sqrt5+1) \Rightarrow \alpha = 5$, $r = \sqrt5$.
$A_1$ is the foot of the perpendicular from $(0, 5)$ to $y = 2x$: $(t, 2t)$ with $t = \dfrac{0 + 10}{5} = 2$, so $A_1 = (2, 4)$.
$B_1 = 2(0, 5) - (2, 4) = (-2, 6)$.
P→4, Q→2, R→5, S→3 → (C).

questions.text:
Let $\gamma \in \mathbb{R}$ be such that the lines $L_1 : \dfrac{x+11}{1} = \dfrac{y+21}{2} = \dfrac{z+29}{3}$ and $L_2 : \dfrac{x+16}{3} = \dfrac{y+11}{2} = \dfrac{z+4}{\gamma}$ intersect. Let $R_1$ be the point of intersection of $L_1$ and $L_2$. Let $O = (0, 0, 0)$, and $\hat{n}$ denote a unit normal vector to the plane containing both the lines $L_1$ and $L_2$.
Match each entry in List-I to the correct entry in List-II.
List-IList-II
(P) $\gamma$ equals(1) $-\hat{i} - \hat{j} + \hat{k}$
(Q) A possible choice for $\hat{n}$ is(2) $\sqrt{\dfrac{3}{2}}$
(R) $\overrightarrow{OR_1}$ equals(3) $1$
(S) A possible value of $\overrightarrow{OR_1} \cdot \hat{n}$ is(4) $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{6}}\hat{i} - \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{6}}\hat{j} + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{6}}\hat{k}$
(5) $\sqrt{\dfrac{2}{3}}$
questions.sol:
Points of $L_1$: $(-11 + t, -21 + 2t, -29 + 3t)$; of $L_2$: $(-16 + 3s, -11 + 2s, -4 + \gamma s)$.
$x$: $t = 3s - 5$; $y$: $2t = 10 + 2s \Rightarrow t = s + 5$. So $s = 5$, $t = 10$, and $R_1 = (-1, -1, 1)$.
$z$: $-29 + 30 = 1 = -4 + 5\gamma \Rightarrow \gamma = 1$.
Normal $\propto (1, 2, 3) \times (3, 2, 1) = (-4, 8, -4) \propto (1, -2, 1)$, so $\hat n = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt6}(\hat i - 2\hat j + \hat k)$.
$\overrightarrow{OR_1}\cdot\hat n = \dfrac{-1 + 2 + 1}{\sqrt6} = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt6} = \sqrt{\dfrac23}$.
P→3, Q→4, R→1, S→5 → (C).

questions.text:
Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ and $g : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be functions defined by $$f(x) = \begin{cases} x|x|\sin\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right), & x \neq 0, \\ 0, & x = 0, \end{cases} \qquad \text{and} \qquad g(x) = \begin{cases} 1 - 2x, & 0 \le x \le \dfrac{1}{2}, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}. \end{cases}$$Let $a, b, c, d \in \mathbb{R}$. Define the function $h : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ by $$h(x) = a\,f(x) + b\left(g(x) + g\left(\frac{1}{2} - x\right)\right) + c\left(x - g(x)\right) + d\,g(x), \quad x \in \mathbb{R}.$$Match each entry in List-I to the correct entry in List-II.
List-IList-II
(P) If $a = 0$, $b = 1$, $c = 0$, and $d = 0$, then(1) $h$ is one-one.
(Q) If $a = 1$, $b = 0$, $c = 0$, and $d = 0$, then(2) $h$ is onto.
(R) If $a = 0$, $b = 0$, $c = 1$, and $d = 0$, then(3) $h$ is differentiable on $\mathbb{R}$.
(S) If $a = 0$, $b = 0$, $c = 0$, and $d = 1$, then(4) the range of $h$ is $[0, 1]$.
(5) the range of $h$ is $\{0, 1\}$.
questions.sol:
(P) $h(x) = g(x) + g\left(\frac12 - x\right)$. For $0 \le x \le \frac12$ both arguments lie in $[0, \frac12]$: $h = (1 - 2x) + 2x = 1$. Otherwise both terms are 0. Range $\{0, 1\}$ → (5).
(Q) $h = f$. For $x \neq 0$, $f$ is differentiable, and $f'(0) = \lim_{x\to0}|x|\sin\frac1x = 0$. So $h$ is differentiable on $\mathbb{R}$ → (3).
(R) $h(x) = x - g(x)$: equal to $x$ for $x \lt 0$ and $x > \frac12$, and $3x - 1$ on $[0, \frac12]$ (from $-1$ to $\frac12$). The pieces cover $(-\infty, 0) \cup [-1, \frac12] \cup (\frac12, \infty) = \mathbb{R}$: onto (not one-one, e.g. $h = -\frac12$ twice) → (2).
(S) $h = g$, with range $[0, 1]$ → (4).
P→5, Q→3, R→2, S→4 → (C).

questions.text: A dimensionless quantity is constructed in terms of electronic charge $e$, permittivity of free space $\varepsilon_0$, Planck's constant $h$, and speed of light $c$. If the dimensionless quantity is written as $e^{\alpha}\varepsilon_0^{\beta}h^{\gamma}c^{\delta}$ and $n$ is a non-zero integer, then $(\alpha, \beta, \gamma, \delta)$ is given by
questions.sol:
$\dfrac{e^2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 r}$ is an energy and $\dfrac{hc}{r}$ is an energy, so $\dfrac{e^2}{\varepsilon_0 hc}$ is dimensionless (it equals twice the fine-structure constant $\dfrac{e^2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0\hbar c}$).
Any power of it is dimensionless: $\left(\dfrac{e^2}{\varepsilon_0 hc}\right)^n = e^{2n}\varepsilon_0^{-n}h^{-n}c^{-n}$.
$(\alpha, \beta, \gamma, \delta) = (2n, -n, -n, -n)$ → (A).

questions.text:
An infinitely long wire, located on the $z$-axis, carries a current $I$ along the $+z$-direction and produces the magnetic field $\vec{B}$. The magnitude of the line integral $\int \vec{B} \cdot \vec{dl}$ along a straight line from the point $(-\sqrt{3}a, a, 0)$ to $(a, a, 0)$ is given by
[$\mu_0$ is the magnetic permeability of free space.]
questions.sol:
$\vec B = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi r}\hat\phi$, so $\vec B\cdot\vec{dl} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi r}\, r\,d\phi = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi}d\phi$: the integral depends only on the angle swept.
Start $(-\sqrt3a, a)$: $\phi = 150^\circ$. End $(a, a)$: $\phi = 45^\circ$. The line ($y = a$) does not cross the wire, so $|\Delta\phi| = 105^\circ = \dfrac{7\pi}{12}$.
$\left|\int\vec B\cdot\vec{dl}\right| = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi}\cdot\dfrac{7\pi}{12} = \dfrac{7\mu_0 I}{24}$ → (A).

questions.text:
Two beads, each with charge $q$ and mass $m$, are on a horizontal, frictionless, non-conducting, circular hoop of radius $R$. One of the beads is glued to the hoop at some point, while the other one performs small oscillations about its equilibrium position along the hoop. The square of the angular frequency of the small oscillations is given by
[$\varepsilon_0$ is the permittivity of free space.]
questions.sol:
Equilibrium: the free bead is diametrically opposite the fixed one.
Displace it by an angle $\theta$ (measured from the centre) along the hoop; the separation becomes $2R\cos\dfrac\theta2$.
$U(\theta) = \dfrac{q^2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0\cdot 2R\cos(\theta/2)} \approx \dfrac{q^2}{8\pi\varepsilon_0 R}\left(1 + \dfrac{\theta^2}{8}\right)$.
Kinetic energy $\dfrac12 mR^2\dot\theta^2$, so $\omega^2 = \dfrac{U''(0)}{mR^2} = \dfrac{q^2/(32\pi\varepsilon_0 R)}{mR^2} = \dfrac{q^2}{32\pi\varepsilon_0 R^3 m}$ → (B).

questions.text: A block of mass 5 kg moves along the $x$-direction subject to the force $F = (-20x + 10)$ N, with the value of $x$ in metre. At time $t = 0$ s, it is at rest at position $x = 1$ m. The position and momentum of the block at $t = (\pi/4)$ s are
questions.sol:
$F = -20(x - 0.5)$: SHM about $x = 0.5$ m with $\omega = \sqrt{20/5} = 2$ rad/s.
Released from rest at $x = 1$ m, so amplitude $0.5$ m: $x = 0.5 + 0.5\cos 2t$, $v = -\sin 2t$ m/s.
At $t = \pi/4$: $x = 0.5$ m, $v = -1$ m/s, $p = 5 \times (-1) = -5$ kg m/s → (C).

questions.text: A particle of mass $m$ is moving in a circular orbit under the influence of the central force $F(r) = -kr$, corresponding to the potential energy $V(r) = kr^2/2$, where $k$ is a positive force constant and $r$ is the radial distance from the origin. According to the Bohr's quantization rule, the angular momentum of the particle is given by $L = n\hbar$, where $\hbar = h/(2\pi)$, $h$ is the Planck's constant, and $n$ a positive integer. If $v$ and $E$ are the speed and total energy of the particle, respectively, then which of the following expression(s) is(are) correct?
questions.sol:
Circular motion: $\dfrac{mv^2}{r} = kr \Rightarrow v = r\sqrt{\dfrac km}$.
$L = mvr = r^2\sqrt{mk} = n\hbar \Rightarrow r^2 = n\hbar\sqrt{\dfrac{1}{mk}}$: (A) correct.
$v^2 = \dfrac{k}{m}r^2 = n\hbar\dfrac{k}{m\sqrt{mk}} = n\hbar\sqrt{\dfrac{k}{m^3}}$: (B) correct.
$\dfrac{L}{mr^2} = \dfrac vr = \sqrt{\dfrac km}$: (C) correct.
$E = \dfrac12mv^2 + \dfrac12kr^2 = kr^2 = n\hbar\sqrt{\dfrac km}$, not half of it: (D) wrong.
Answer: (A), (B), (C).

questions.text: Two uniform strings of mass per unit length $\mu$ and $4\mu$, and length $L$ and $2L$, respectively, are joined at point O, and tied at two fixed ends P and Q, as shown in the figure. The strings are under a uniform tension $T$. If we define the frequency $\nu_0 = \dfrac{1}{2L}\sqrt{\dfrac{T}{\mu}}$, which of the following statement(s) is(are) correct?
options: With a node at O, the minimum frequency of vibration of the composite string is $\nu_0$.
With an antinode at O, the minimum frequency of vibration of the composite string is $2\nu_0$.
When the composite string vibrates at the minimum frequency with a node at O, it has 6 nodes, including the end nodes.

questions.text: A glass beaker has a solid, plano-convex base of refractive index 1.60, as shown in the figure. The radius of curvature of the convex surface (SPU) is 9 cm, while the planar surface (STU) acts as a mirror. This beaker is filled with a liquid of refractive index $n$ up to the level QPR. If the image of a point object O at a height of $h$ (OT in the figure) is formed onto itself, then, which of the following option(s) is(are) correct?
questions.sol:
The image coincides with the object when the rays strike the plane mirror STU normally, i.e. travel parallel to the axis inside the glass.
On the axis the liquid layer has zero thickness at P (the liquid level touches the vertex), so the flat air–liquid surface adds no power; only the liquid–glass curved surface ($R = 9$ cm) refracts.
Image at infinity in glass: $\dfrac{1.6}{\infty} - \dfrac{1}{-h} = \dfrac{1.6 - n}{9} \Rightarrow h = \dfrac{9}{1.6 - n}$ cm.
$n = 1.42$: $h = 50$ cm ✓. $n = 1.35$: $h = 36$ cm ✓. $n = 1.45$: $h = 60$ cm (not 65). $n = 1.48$: $h = 75$ cm (not 85).
Answer: (A), (B).

If the heat required to raise the temperature of 1 kg of the substance from $-73\ ^\circ$C to $27\ ^\circ$C is $nk$, the value of $n$ is _____.

questions.text: A disc of mass $M$ and radius $R$ is free to rotate about its vertical axis as shown in the figure. A battery operated motor of negligible mass is fixed to this disc at a point on its circumference. Another disc of the same mass $M$ and radius $R/2$ is fixed to the motor's thin shaft. Initially, both the discs are at rest. The motor is switched on so that the smaller disc rotates at a uniform angular speed $\omega$. If the angular speed at which the large disc rotates is $\omega/n$, then the value of $n$ is _____.
questions.sol:
No external torque about the large disc's axis, so the total angular momentum about it stays zero.
Small disc spin: $\dfrac12 M\left(\dfrac R2\right)^2\omega = \dfrac{MR^2\omega}{8}$.
Large disc rotating at $\Omega$ (opposite sense) carries the small disc's centre round a circle of radius $R$: $\left(\dfrac12MR^2 + MR^2\right)\Omega = \dfrac32MR^2\Omega$.
$\dfrac32MR^2\Omega = \dfrac{MR^2\omega}{8} \Rightarrow \Omega = \dfrac{\omega}{12}$, so $n = 12$.

questions.text: A point source S emits unpolarized light uniformly in all directions. At two points A and B, the ratio $r = I_A/I_B$ of the intensities of light is 2. If a set of two polaroids having $45^\circ$ angle between their pass-axes is placed just before point B, then the new value of $r$ will be _____.
questions.sol:
First polaroid: unpolarized light is halved, $I_B/2$.
Second polaroid (Malus): $\dfrac{I_B}{2}\cos^2 45^\circ = \dfrac{I_B}{4}$.
New $r = \dfrac{I_A}{I_B/4} = 4 \times 2 = 8$.

questions.text: A source (S) of sound has frequency 240 Hz. When the observer (O) and the source move towards each other at a speed $v$ with respect to the ground (as shown in Case 1 in the figure), the observer measures the frequency of the sound to be 288 Hz. However, when the observer and the source move away from each other at the same speed $v$ with respect to the ground (as shown in Case 2 in the figure), the observer measures the frequency of sound to be $n$ Hz. The value of $n$ is _____.
questions.sol:
Case 1 (approaching): $288 = 240\,\dfrac{c + v}{c - v} \Rightarrow \dfrac{c + v}{c - v} = 1.2$ (with $c$ the speed of sound).
Case 2 (receding): $n = 240\,\dfrac{c - v}{c + v} = \dfrac{240}{1.2} = 200$.

questions.text: Two large, identical water tanks, 1 and 2, kept on the top of a building of height $H$, are filled with water up to height $h$ in each tank. Both the tanks contain an identical hole of small radius on their sides, close to their bottom. A pipe of the same internal radius as that of the hole is connected to tank 2, and the pipe ends at the ground level. When the water flows from the tanks 1 and 2 through the holes, the times taken to empty the tanks are $t_1$ and $t_2$, respectively. If $H = \left(\dfrac{16}{9}\right)h$, then the ratio $t_1/t_2$ is _____.
questions.sol:
Tank area $A$, hole area $a$, water depth $y$. $A\dfrac{dy}{dt} = -a v$.
Tank 1: $v = \sqrt{2gy}$, so $t_1 = \dfrac Aa\displaystyle\int_0^h\dfrac{dy}{\sqrt{2gy}} = \dfrac{A}{a}\cdot\dfrac{2\sqrt h}{\sqrt{2g}}$.
Tank 2: water leaves at the pipe end, a height $y + H$ below the surface: $v = \sqrt{2g(y + H)}$, so $t_2 = \dfrac Aa\cdot\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{2g}}\left(\sqrt{h + H} - \sqrt H\right)$.
$\dfrac{t_1}{t_2} = \dfrac{\sqrt h}{\sqrt{h + H} - \sqrt H} = \dfrac{\sqrt h}{\frac53\sqrt h - \frac43\sqrt h} = 3$.

questions.text: A thin uniform rod of length $L$ and certain mass is kept on a frictionless horizontal table with a massless string of length $L$ fixed to one end (top view is shown in the figure). The other end of the string is pivoted to a point O. If a horizontal impulse $P$ is imparted to the rod at a distance $x = L/n$ from the mid-point of the rod (see figure), then the rod and string revolve together around the point O, with the rod remaining aligned with the string. In such a case, the value of $n$ is _____.
questions.sol:
The rod's centre is at $\dfrac{3L}{2}$ from O. To move with the string, the rod must rotate about O with some $\omega$: $v_{cm} = \dfrac{3L}{2}\omega$.
The string's impulse acts along the rod through the centre, so it has no effect on rotation about the centre and none perpendicular to the rod.
Linear: $P = m\cdot\dfrac{3L}{2}\omega$. Angular about the centre: $Px = \dfrac{mL^2}{12}\omega$.
Dividing: $x = \dfrac{L^2/12}{3L/2} = \dfrac{L}{18}$, so $n = 18$.

questions.text:
One mole of a monatomic ideal gas undergoes the cyclic process J $\to$ K $\to$ L $\to$ M $\to$ J, as shown in the P-T diagram.
Match the quantities mentioned in List-I with their values in List-II and choose the correct option.
[$\mathcal{R}$ is the gas constant.]
List-IList-II
(P) Work done in the complete cyclic process(1) $\mathcal{R}T_0 - 4\mathcal{R}T_0\ln 2$
(Q) Change in the internal energy of the gas in the process JK(2) $0$
(R) Heat given to the gas in the process KL(3) $3\mathcal{R}T_0$
(S) Change in the internal energy of the gas in the process MJ(4) $-2\mathcal{R}T_0\ln 2$
(5) $-3\mathcal{R}T_0\ln 2$
questions.sol:
JK: isobaric at $P_0$, $T_0 \to 3T_0$: $W = \mathcal R(2T_0)$, $\Delta U = \dfrac32\mathcal R(2T_0) = 3\mathcal RT_0$.
KL: isothermal at $3T_0$, $P_0 \to 2P_0$: $W = 3\mathcal RT_0\ln\dfrac{P_0}{2P_0} = -3\mathcal RT_0\ln2 = Q$.
LM: isobaric at $2P_0$, $3T_0 \to T_0$: $W = -2\mathcal RT_0$.
MJ: isothermal at $T_0$, $2P_0 \to P_0$: $W = \mathcal RT_0\ln2$, $\Delta U = 0$.
Net work $= 2\mathcal RT_0 - 3\mathcal RT_0\ln2 - 2\mathcal RT_0 + \mathcal RT_0\ln2 = -2\mathcal RT_0\ln2$.
P→4, Q→3, R→5, S→2 → (B).

questions.text:
Four identical thin, square metal sheets, $S_1$, $S_2$, $S_3$ and $S_4$, each of side $a$ are kept parallel to each other with equal distance $d\ (\ll a)$ between them, as shown in the figure. Let $C_0 = \varepsilon_0 a^2/d$, where $\varepsilon_0$ is the permittivity of free space.
Match the quantities mentioned in List-I with their values in List-II and choose the correct option.
List-IList-II
(P) The capacitance between $S_1$ and $S_4$, with $S_2$ and $S_3$ not connected, is(1) $3C_0$
(Q) The capacitance between $S_1$ and $S_4$, with $S_2$ shorted to $S_3$, is(2) $C_0/2$
(R) The capacitance between $S_1$ and $S_3$, with $S_2$ shorted to $S_4$, is(3) $C_0/3$
(S) The capacitance between $S_1$ and $S_2$, with $S_3$ shorted to $S_1$, and $S_2$ shorted to $S_4$, is(4) $2C_0/3$
(5) $2C_0$
questions.sol:
Each gap between neighbouring sheets is a capacitor $C_0$.
(P) Three gaps in series: $C_0/3$ → (3).
(Q) The $S_2$–$S_3$ gap is shorted (no field); $S_1S_2$ and $S_3S_4$ in series: $C_0/2$ → (2).
(R) Node $A = S_1$, node $B = \{S_2, S_4\}$, node $S_3$. $S_1S_2$: $C_0$ between $A$ and $B$. $S_2S_3$ and $S_3S_4$: both between $B$ and $S_3$, in parallel ($2C_0$). Series: $\dfrac{C_0\cdot2C_0}{3C_0} = \dfrac{2C_0}{3}$ → (4).
(S) Nodes $\{S_1, S_3\}$ and $\{S_2, S_4\}$: all three gaps lie between these two nodes, in parallel: $3C_0$ → (1).
P→3, Q→2, R→4, S→1 → (C).

questions.text:
A light ray is incident on the surface of a sphere of refractive index $n$ at an angle of incidence $\theta_0$. The ray partially refracts into the sphere with angle of refraction $\phi_0$ and then partly reflects from the back surface. The reflected ray then emerges out of the sphere after a partial refraction. The total angle of deviation of the emergent ray with respect to the incident ray is $\alpha$. Match the quantities mentioned in List-I with their values in List-II and choose the correct option.
List-IList-II
(P) If $n = 2$ and $\alpha = 180^\circ$, then all the possible values of $\theta_0$ will be(1) $30^\circ$ and $0^\circ$
(Q) If $n = \sqrt{3}$ and $\alpha = 180^\circ$, then all the possible values of $\theta_0$ will be(2) $60^\circ$ and $0^\circ$
(R) If $n = \sqrt{3}$ and $\alpha = 180^\circ$, then all the possible values of $\phi_0$ will be(3) $45^\circ$ and $0^\circ$
(S) If $n = \sqrt{2}$ and $\theta_0 = 45^\circ$, then all the possible values of $\alpha$ will be(4) $150^\circ$
(5) $0^\circ$
questions.sol:
Deviation: $(\theta_0 - \phi_0)$ at entry, $(180^\circ - 2\phi_0)$ at the reflection, $(\theta_0 - \phi_0)$ at exit: $\alpha = 180^\circ + 2\theta_0 - 4\phi_0$.
$\alpha = 180^\circ \Rightarrow \theta_0 = 2\phi_0$; with $\sin\theta_0 = n\sin\phi_0$: $2\sin\phi_0\cos\phi_0 = n\sin\phi_0$, so $\phi_0 = 0$ or $\cos\phi_0 = \dfrac n2$.
(P) $n = 2$: $\cos\phi_0 = 1$ gives $\phi_0 = 0$ only, so $\theta_0 = 0^\circ$ → (5).
(Q), (R) $n = \sqrt3$: $\phi_0 = 0^\circ$ or $30^\circ$, so $\theta_0 = 0^\circ$ or $60^\circ$. Q → (2), R → (1).
(S) $n = \sqrt2$, $\theta_0 = 45^\circ$: $\sin\phi_0 = \dfrac12$, $\phi_0 = 30^\circ$; $\alpha = 180^\circ + 90^\circ - 120^\circ = 150^\circ$ → (4).
P→5, Q→2, R→1, S→4 → (A).

questions.text:
The circuit shown in the figure contains an inductor $L$, a capacitor $C_0$, a resistor $R_0$ and an ideal battery. The circuit also contains two keys $K_1$ and $K_2$. Initially, both the keys are open and there is no charge on the capacitor. At an instant, key $K_1$ is closed and immediately after this the current in $R_0$ is found to be $I_1$. After a long time, the current attains a steady state value $I_2$. Thereafter, $K_2$ is closed and simultaneously $K_1$ is opened and the voltage across $C_0$ oscillates with amplitude $V_0$ and angular frequency $\omega_0$.
Match the quantities mentioned in List-I with their values in List-II and choose the correct option.
List-IList-II
(P) The value of $I_1$ in Ampere is(1) $0$
(Q) The value of $I_2$ in Ampere is(2) $2$
(R) The value of $\omega_0$ in kilo-radians/s is(3) $4$
(S) The value of $V_0$ in Volt is(4) $20$
(5) $200$
questions.sol:
With $K_1$ closed ($K_2$ open) the battery, $R_0$ and $L$ form a series circuit.
Just after closing, the inductor blocks any sudden current: $I_1 = 0$ → (1).
Steady state: $I_2 = \dfrac{20}{5} = 4$ A → (3).
Then $L$ and $C_0$ form an isolated LC loop: $\omega_0 = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{LC_0}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{25\times10^{-3}\times10\times10^{-6}}} = 2000$ rad/s $= 2$ krad/s → (2).
Energy: $\dfrac12LI_2^2 = \dfrac12C_0V_0^2 \Rightarrow V_0 = I_2\sqrt{\dfrac{L}{C_0}} = 4\sqrt{2500} = 200$ V → (5).
P→1, Q→3, R→2, S→5 → (A).

questions.text: A closed vessel contains 10 g of an ideal gas X at 300 K, which exerts 2 atm pressure. At the same temperature, 80 g of another ideal gas Y is added to it and the pressure becomes 6 atm. The ratio of root mean square velocities of X and Y at 300 K is
questions.sol:
Same $V$ and $T$: partial pressures are proportional to moles. $p_X = 2$ atm, $p_Y = 6 - 2 = 4$ atm, so $n_Y = 2n_X$.
$\dfrac{80}{M_Y} = 2\cdot\dfrac{10}{M_X} \Rightarrow M_Y = 4M_X$.
$\dfrac{u_X}{u_Y} = \sqrt{\dfrac{M_Y}{M_X}} = 2$, i.e. $2 : 1$ → (D).

questions.text: At room temperature, disproportionation of an aqueous solution of in situ generated nitrous acid ($\mathrm{HNO_2}$) gives the species

questions.text:
Aspartame, an artificial sweetener, is a dipeptide aspartyl phenylalanine methyl ester. The structure of aspartame is
Structures of phenylalanine and aspartic acid are given below.

questions.text:
Among the following options, select the option in which each complex in Set-I shows geometrical isomerism and the two complexes in Set-II are ionization isomers of each other.
[en = $\mathrm{H_2NCH_2CH_2NH_2}$]
questions.sol:
(A) $\mathrm{[Ni(CO)_4]}$ is tetrahedral: no geometrical isomers. Rejected.
(B) Set-II differ by exchange of metals between cation and anion: coordination isomers, not ionization isomers. Rejected.
(D) $\mathrm{[Cr(NH_3)_5Cl]^{2+}}$ ($\mathrm{MA_5B}$) has no geometrical isomers, and Set-II are hydrate isomers. Rejected.
(C) $\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_3(NO_2)_3]}$ has fac/mer isomers and $\mathrm{[Co(en)_2Cl_2]^+}$ has cis/trans isomers; in Set-II, $\mathrm{Cl^-}$ and $\mathrm{SO_4^{2-}}$ swap between the coordination sphere and the counter-ion: ionization isomers → (C).

questions.text: Among the following, the correct statement(s) for electrons in an atom is(are)
options: Uncertainty principle rules out the existence of definite paths for electrons.
The energy of an electron in $2s$ orbital of an atom is lower than the energy of an electron that is infinitely far away from the nucleus.
According to Bohr's model, the most negative energy value for an electron is given by n = 1, which corresponds to the most stable orbit.
According to Bohr's model, the magnitude of velocity of electrons increases with increase in values of n.
questions.sol:
(A) Position and momentum cannot both be exactly known, so a definite trajectory is meaningless. Correct.
(B) A bound electron has negative energy; a free electron at infinity has zero energy. Correct.
(C) $E_n \propto -\dfrac{1}{n^2}$ is most negative for $n = 1$, the most stable orbit. Correct.
(D) $v_n \propto \dfrac{Z}{n}$ decreases as $n$ increases. Wrong.
Answer: (A), (B), (C).

questions.text:
Reaction of iso-propylbenzene with $\mathrm{O_2}$ followed by the treatment with $\mathrm{H_3O^+}$ forms phenol and a by-product P. Reaction of P with 3 equivalents of $\mathrm{Cl_2}$ gives compound Q. Treatment of Q with $\mathrm{Ca(OH)_2}$ produces compound R and calcium salt S.
The correct statement(s) regarding P, Q, R and S is(are)
options: Reaction of P with R in the presence of KOH followed by acidification gives $\mathrm{(H_3C)_2C(OH)CCl_3}$
Reaction of R with $\mathrm{O_2}$ in the presence of light gives phosgene gas
Q reacts with aqueous NaOH to produce $\mathrm{Cl_3CCH_2OH}$ and $\mathrm{Cl_3CCOONa}$
questions.sol:
Cumene process: P = acetone, $\mathrm{CH_3COCH_3}$.
Q = $\mathrm{CH_3COCCl_3}$ (α-chlorination of the methyl group).
$\mathrm{Ca(OH)_2}$ cleaves Q (haloform): R = $\mathrm{CHCl_3}$, S = $\mathrm{(CH_3COO)_2Ca}$.
(A) $\mathrm{CCl_3^-}$ (from $\mathrm{CHCl_3}$ + KOH) adds to acetone; acidification gives chloretone, $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2C(OH)CCl_3}$. Correct.
(B) $2\mathrm{CHCl_3} + \mathrm{O_2} \xrightarrow{h\nu} 2\mathrm{COCl_2} + 2\mathrm{HCl}$. Correct.
(C) Q with NaOH gives $\mathrm{CHCl_3}$ and $\mathrm{CH_3COONa}$, not those products. Wrong.
(D) Dry distillation of calcium acetate gives acetone. Correct.
Answer: (A), (B), (D).

questions.text: The option(s) in which at least three molecules follow Octet Rule is(are)

Follow the octet rule: $\mathrm{CO_2}$, $\mathrm{C_2H_4}$, HCl, $\mathrm{O_3}$.
Do not: NO and $\mathrm{NO_2}$ (odd-electron molecules), $\mathrm{BCl_3}$ (B has only 6 electrons), $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ (S has an expanded octet).

(B) $\mathrm{O_3}$, HCl: two. ✗ (C) none. ✗
(D) $\mathrm{CO_2}$, $\mathrm{O_3}$, $\mathrm{C_2H_4}$: three. ✓
Answer: (A), (D).

questions.text:
Consider the following volume$-$temperature (V$-$T) diagram for the expansion of 5 moles of an ideal monoatomic gas.
Considering only P-V work is involved, the total change in enthalpy (in Joule) for the transformation of state in the sequence X$\to$Y$\to$Z is ______.
[Use the given data: Molar heat capacity of the gas for the given temperature range, $C_{V,m} = 12$ J K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$ and gas constant, $R = 8.3$ J K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$]
questions.note: Official final key: 8000 or 8120 or 8300 (any of these values is awarded marks).
questions.sol:
For an ideal gas $H$ depends only on $T$.
X → Y is at constant $T$ (335 K): $\Delta H = 0$.
Y → Z: $T$ rises from 335 K to 415 K, $\Delta T = 80$ K. $C_{p,m} = C_{V,m} + R = 12 + 8.3 = 20.3$ J K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$.
$\Delta H = nC_{p,m}\Delta T = 5 \times 20.3 \times 80 = 8120$ J.
The official key also accepts 8000 and 8300 (for example $C_{p,m} = \dfrac52R = 20.75$ gives 8300).

questions.text: Consider the following reaction, $$\mathrm{2H_2(g) + 2NO(g) \longrightarrow N_2(g) + 2H_2O(g)}$$ which follows the mechanism given below: $$\mathrm{2NO(g)} \underset{k_{-1}}{\overset{k_1}{\rightleftharpoons}} \mathrm{N_2O_2(g)} \qquad (\text{fast equilibrium})$$ $$\mathrm{N_2O_2(g) + H_2(g)} \xrightarrow{k_2} \mathrm{N_2O(g) + H_2O(g)} \qquad (\text{slow reaction})$$ $$\mathrm{N_2O(g) + H_2(g)} \xrightarrow{k_3} \mathrm{N_2(g) + H_2O(g)} \qquad (\text{fast reaction})$$The order of the reaction is ______.
questions.sol:
Rate is set by the slow step: rate $= k_2[\mathrm{N_2O_2}][\mathrm{H_2}]$.
Fast equilibrium: $[\mathrm{N_2O_2}] = \dfrac{k_1}{k_{-1}}[\mathrm{NO}]^2$.
Rate $= \dfrac{k_1k_2}{k_{-1}}[\mathrm{NO}]^2[\mathrm{H_2}]$: order $2 + 1 = 3$.

questions.text:
Complete reaction of acetaldehyde with excess formaldehyde, upon heating with conc. NaOH solution, gives P and Q. Compound P does not give Tollens' test, whereas Q on acidification gives positive Tollens' test. Treatment of P with excess cyclohexanone in the presence of catalytic amount of p-toluenesulfonic acid (PTSA) gives product R.
Sum of the number of methylene groups (-CH$_2$-) and oxygen atoms in R is ______.
questions.sol:
Three crossed aldols: $\mathrm{CH_3CHO} + 3\mathrm{HCHO} \to \mathrm{(HOCH_2)_3C{-}CHO}$; then crossed Cannizzaro with HCHO gives P = pentaerythritol $\mathrm{C(CH_2OH)_4}$ and Q = $\mathrm{HCOONa}$ (formic acid on acidification, Tollens positive).
P + excess cyclohexanone (PTSA): each pair of $\mathrm{CH_2OH}$ groups forms a cyclic ketal, giving a dispiro bis-ketal R: $\mathrm{C(CH_2O)_4}$ bridged by two cyclohexylidene units.
$\mathrm{CH_2}$ groups: 4 (from pentaerythritol) + $2 \times 5$ (cyclohexane rings) = 14. Oxygen atoms: 4.
Sum $= 18$.

questions.text:
Among $\mathrm{V(CO)_6}$, $\mathrm{Cr(CO)_5}$, $\mathrm{Cu(CO)_3}$, $\mathrm{Mn(CO)_5}$, $\mathrm{Fe(CO)_5}$, $\mathrm{[Co(CO)_3]^{3-}}$, $\mathrm{[Cr(CO)_4]^{4-}}$, and $\mathrm{Ir(CO)_3}$, the total number of species isoelectronic with $\mathrm{Ni(CO)_4}$ is ______.
[Given, atomic number: V = 23, Cr = 24, Mn = 25, Fe = 26, Co = 27, Ni = 28, Cu = 29, Ir = 77]
questions.sol:
Compare the valence electron count (metal electrons + 2 per CO + negative charge). $\mathrm{Ni(CO)_4}$: $10 + 8 = 18$.
$\mathrm{V(CO)_6}$: $5 + 12 = 17$. $\mathrm{Cr(CO)_5}$: $6 + 10 = 16$. $\mathrm{Cu(CO)_3}$: $11 + 6 = 17$. $\mathrm{Mn(CO)_5}$: $7 + 10 = 17$.
$\mathrm{Fe(CO)_5}$: $8 + 10 = 18$ ✓. $\mathrm{[Co(CO)_3]^{3-}}$: $9 + 6 + 3 = 18$ ✓. $\mathrm{[Cr(CO)_4]^{4-}}$: $6 + 8 + 4 = 18$ ✓. $\mathrm{Ir(CO)_3}$: $9 + 6 = 15$.
Number of species $= 3$.

questions.text:
In the following reaction sequence, the major product P is formed.
Glycerol reacts completely with excess P in the presence of an acid catalyst to form Q. Reaction of Q with excess NaOH followed by the treatment with $\mathrm{CaCl_2}$ yields Ca-soap R, quantitatively. Starting with one mole of Q, the amount of R produced in gram is ______.
[Given, atomic weight: H = 1, C = 12, N = 14, O = 16, Na = 23, Cl = 35, Ca = 40]
questions.sol:
Start: $\mathrm{HC{\equiv}C(CH_2)_{15}CO_2Et}$.
(i) $\mathrm{Hg^{2+}/H_3O^+}$ hydrates the terminal alkyne to the methyl ketone $\mathrm{CH_3CO(CH_2)_{15}CO_2Et}$.
(ii) Clemmensen reduction: C=O → $\mathrm{CH_2}$, giving $\mathrm{CH_3(CH_2)_{16}CO_2Et}$. (iii) Ester hydrolysis: P = stearic acid $\mathrm{C_{17}H_{35}COOH}$.
Q = glyceryl tristearate. Saponification gives 3 mol $\mathrm{C_{17}H_{35}COO^-}$, which form 1.5 mol R = $\mathrm{(C_{17}H_{35}COO)_2Ca}$.
$M(\mathrm{R}) = 2 \times 283 + 40 = 606$; mass $= 1.5 \times 606 = 909$ g.

questions.text:
Among the following complexes, the total number of diamagnetic species is ______.
$\mathrm{[Mn(NH_3)_6]^{3+}}$, $\mathrm{[MnCl_6]^{3-}}$, $\mathrm{[FeF_6]^{3-}}$, $\mathrm{[CoF_6]^{3-}}$, $\mathrm{[Fe(NH_3)_6]^{3+}}$, and $\mathrm{[Co(en)_3]^{3+}}$
[Given, atomic number: Mn = 25, Fe = 26, Co = 27; en = $\mathrm{H_2NCH_2CH_2NH_2}$]
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{Mn^{3+}}$ ($d^4$): unpaired electrons in both $\mathrm{[Mn(NH_3)_6]^{3+}}$ and $\mathrm{[MnCl_6]^{3-}}$ (2 or 4, never 0): paramagnetic.
$\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$ ($d^5$): always at least one unpaired electron: $\mathrm{[FeF_6]^{3-}}$ and $\mathrm{[Fe(NH_3)_6]^{3+}}$ paramagnetic.
$\mathrm{Co^{3+}}$ ($d^6$): $\mathrm{F^-}$ is a weak field ligand, high spin $t_{2g}^4e_g^2$: paramagnetic. en is a strong field ligand, low spin $t_{2g}^6$: diamagnetic.
Only $\mathrm{[Co(en)_3]^{3+}}$ is diamagnetic: answer $1$.

questions.text:
In a conductometric titration, small volume of titrant of higher concentration is added stepwise to a larger volume of titrate of much lower concentration, and the conductance is measured after each addition.
The limiting ionic conductivity ($\Lambda_0$) values (in mS m$^2$ mol$^{-1}$) for different ions in aqueous solutions are given below:
$\mathrm{Ag^+}$: 6.2, $\mathrm{K^+}$: 7.4, $\mathrm{Na^+}$: 5.0, $\mathrm{H^+}$: 35.0, $\mathrm{NO_3^-}$: 7.2, $\mathrm{Cl^-}$: 7.6, $\mathrm{SO_4^{2-}}$: 16.0, $\mathrm{OH^-}$: 19.9, $\mathrm{CH_3COO^-}$: 4.1
For different combinations of titrates and titrants given in List-I, the graphs of 'conductance' versus 'volume of titrant' are given in List-II (see the figure).
Match each entry in List-I with the appropriate entry in List-II and choose the correct option.
List-IList-II
(P) Titrate: KCl; Titrant: $\mathrm{AgNO_3}$(1) Graph (1) in the figure
(Q) Titrate: $\mathrm{AgNO_3}$; Titrant: KCl(2) Graph (2) in the figure
(R) Titrate: NaOH; Titrant: HCl(3) Graph (3) in the figure
(S) Titrate: NaOH; Titrant: $\mathrm{CH_3COOH}$(4) Graph (4) in the figure
(5) Graph (5) in the figure
questions.sol:
(P) $\mathrm{Cl^-}$ (7.6) is replaced by $\mathrm{NO_3^-}$ (7.2) as AgCl precipitates: slight fall; after the end point $\mathrm{Ag^+}$ and $\mathrm{NO_3^-}$ add: rise → graph (3).
(Q) $\mathrm{Ag^+}$ (6.2) is replaced by $\mathrm{K^+}$ (7.4): slight rise; after the end point $\mathrm{K^+}$ and $\mathrm{Cl^-}$ add: steeper rise → graph (4).
(R) $\mathrm{OH^-}$ (19.9) is replaced by $\mathrm{Cl^-}$ (7.6): steep fall; after the end point $\mathrm{H^+}$ (35.0) and $\mathrm{Cl^-}$ add: steep rise → graph (2).
(S) $\mathrm{OH^-}$ is replaced by $\mathrm{CH_3COO^-}$ (4.1): fall; after the end point the weak acid hardly ionises: nearly flat → graph (5).
P-3, Q-4, R-2, S-5 → (C).

Based on VSEPR model, match the xenon compounds given in List-I with the corresponding geometries and the number of lone pairs on xenon given in List-II and choose the correct option.
List-IList-II
(P) $\mathrm{XeF_2}$(1) Trigonal bipyramidal and two lone pair of electrons
(Q) $\mathrm{XeF_4}$(2) Tetrahedral and one lone pair of electrons
(R) $\mathrm{XeO_3}$(3) Octahedral and two lone pair of electrons
(S) $\mathrm{XeO_3F_2}$(4) Trigonal bipyramidal and no lone pair of electrons
(5) Trigonal bipyramidal and three lone pair of electrons
questions.sol:
Electron-pair geometry (VSEPR) and lone pairs on Xe:
$\mathrm{XeF_2}$: 2 bond pairs + 3 lone pairs = 5 pairs, trigonal bipyramidal, three lone pairs → (5).
$\mathrm{XeF_4}$: 4 + 2 = 6 pairs, octahedral, two lone pairs → (3).
$\mathrm{XeO_3}$: 3 σ bond pairs + 1 lone pair = 4 pairs, tetrahedral, one lone pair → (2).
$\mathrm{XeO_3F_2}$: 5 σ bond pairs, no lone pair, trigonal bipyramidal → (4).
P-5, Q-3, R-2, S-4 → (B).

questions.sol:
(P) Cyclohexene + $\mathrm{O_3}$/Zn → hexanedial; aq. NaOH, Δ: intramolecular aldol and dehydration → cyclopent-1-ene-1-carbaldehyde. Ethylene glycol/PTSA protects CHO as an acetal; hydroboration–oxidation puts OH on the ring carbon next to the acetal carbon (anti-Markovnikov); $\mathrm{H_3O^+}$ frees CHO; $\mathrm{NaBH_4}$ reduces it to $\mathrm{CH_2OH}$: 2-(hydroxymethyl)cyclopentanol → (3).
(Q) 1-Methylcyclohexene + $\mathrm{O_3}$/Zn → 6-oxoheptanal; aldol (ketone α-$\mathrm{CH_2}$ attacking CHO, five-membered ring) and dehydration → 1-acetylcyclopentene. Same steps: ketal, hydroboration (OH on the adjacent ring carbon), deprotection, reduction of C=O: 1-(2-hydroxycyclopentyl)ethanol → (5).
(R) 2-Methylcyclopent-2-enone: protect C=O; oxymercuration–demercuration adds OH to the more substituted carbon (the one bearing $\mathrm{CH_3}$); deprotect and reduce: 1-methylcyclopentane-1,2-diol → (4).
(S) Same, but hydroboration–oxidation puts OH on the less substituted carbon: after deprotection and reduction, 2-methylcyclopentane-1,3-diol → (1).
P-3, Q-5, R-4, S-1 → (A).
